claim: In 1893 Muir campaigns for creation of Mount Rainier National Park.

evidence.quote:
1893
April 21 : John Muir turns 55 years old
May: Muir takes East Coast trip
Muir stops for nearly a week at the Chicago World's Fair; finding it "a cosmopolitan rat's nest." (In Wolfe, Son of the Wilderness). In a letter to his wife Louie, he expanded on his assessment: "I ...have seen the best of it though months would be required to see it all. You know I called it a cosmopolitan rats nest containing much rubbish & common place stuff as well as things novel & precious. Well, now that I have seen it, it seems just such a rats nest still, & what do you think was one of the first things I saw when I entered the nearest of the huge buildings. A huge rats nest in a glass case about 8 feet square, with stuffed wood rats looking out from the mass of sticks & leaves etc. natural as life. So you see as usual I am [always?] right! I most enjoyed the art galleries. There are about eighteen acres of paintings by every nation under the sun & I wandered & gazed until I was ready to fall down with utter exhaustion. The art gallery of the California building is quite small & of little significance, not more than a dozen or two of paintings all told – 4 by Keith, not his best, & 4 by Hill not his best, & a few others of no special character by others except a good small one by Yelland. But the national galleries are perfectly overwhelming in grandeur & bulk & variety... The outside view of the buildings is grand & also beautiful. For the best architects have done their best in building them while Frederick Law Olmstead laid out the grounds. Last night the buildings & terraces & fountains along the canals were illuminated by tens of thousands of electric lights arranged along miles of lines of gables, domes & cornices with glorious effect. it was all fairyland on a scale & would have made the Queen of Sheba & poor Solomon in all their glory feel sick with helpless envy." Letter from John Muir to Louie[Strentzel Muir, 1893 May 29.
In New York, Century editor Robert Underwood Johnson takes Muir on a succession of luncheons and champagne dinners in his honor. Muir remarks in a letter home: "I had no idea I was so well known, considering how little I have written."
Through Robert Underwood Johnson, meets Henry Fairfield Osborn, the paleontologist, along with Charles S Sargent, Charles Anderson. Dana, Mark Twain, Thomas Bailey Aldrich, Charles Dudley Warner, Rudyard Kipling, George W . Cable, and Nicola Tesla.
June 8 : Visits Concord, Massachusetts and lays flowers on Thoreau's and Emerson's graves; visits Walden Pond
June: Meets John Burroughs for the first time.
Trip to Europe: Edinburgh, Dunbar, London, Ireland, Norway, Switzerland, France, and Italy.
Upon his return from Europe, goes with Robert Underwood Johnson to Washington, D.C., to lobby the Secretary of the Interior Hoke Smith, and other governmental leaders, including Senator Perkins..
Campaigns for creation of Mount Rainier National Park.

John Muir, The Life and Letters and Other Writings , edited and introduced by Terry Gifford, is published (Baton Wicks Publishing). Over 1000 pages long, it contains much previously unpublished material.
The John Muir Trust announces the launch of its John Muir Award

notes: IHH page gives 1997 for the award's creation.

claim: In 1998 the U.S. Postal Service releases its second commemorative postage stamp of John Muir as part of its "Celebrate the Century" stamp program.

evidence.quote:
1998
U.S. Postal Service releases its second commemorative postage stamp of John Muir as part of its "Celebrate the Century" stamp program.

notes: Confirms a 1998 stamp; gives no denomination (IHH says 32-cent).

claim: Grace S. Lindsley recalled that Muir, in his room on the University of Wisconsin campus in Madison in the early 1860s, had invented a combination bed/alarm clock that tipped him onto the floor each morning.

evidence.quote:
1935
Grace S. Lindsley writes Recollections of John Muir, (off-site link) recalling visiting John Muir in his room on the University of Wisconsin campus in Madison in the early 1860s. She describes how he had invented a combination bed/alarm clock that tipped him onto the floor each morning

notes: A 1935 recollection reported by the Sierra Club chronology, not a contemporary record. Bears on the IHH alarm-clock bed claim ('early 1860s').

title: John Muir's Clockwork Desk
notes: Wisconsin Historical Society essay on the desk it holds, on its legacy site (the www.wisconsinhistory.org address returned 404). Not in the authority registry, so secondary.

claim: Muir built a clockwork study desk while at the University of Wisconsin, Madison, 1861-1863.

evidence.quote: Clockwork study desk built by naturalist John Muir while at the University of Wisconsin, Madison, 1861-1863.

notes: Held by the Wisconsin Historical Society as museum object F1998.85.1. The IHH page says the alarm clock bed is on display there; this page shows the desk, and the bed's display is not confirmed.

claim: Muir emigrated with his family in 1849, settling at Fountain Lake, near Portage, Wisconsin.

evidence.quote: Born in Scotland, John Muir emigrated with his family in 1849, settling at Fountain Lake, near Portage, Wisconsin.

1849
April 21 : John Muir turns 11 years old
February : The Muir family emigrates from Glasgow to New York, the trip taking six weeks by sailing ship, then via the Great Lakes and wagon to Fountain Lake , Buffalo Township, Marquette County, Wisconsin.

claim: On the farm Muir constructed water-wheels, thermometers, hygrometers, clocks, automatic horse feeders, and an "early-rising machine," a device that dumped the sleeper out of bed at an appointed time.

evidence.quote: On the farm Muir constructed numerous devices including water-wheels, thermometers, hygrometers, clocks, automatic horse feeders, and an "early-rising machine," a device that dumped the sleeper out of bed at an appointed time

notes: Compare IHH's list for 1854 (locks, water wheels, barometers, hydrometers, clocks, horse-feeding machine); this source gives no year.

title: John Muir papers, 1849-1957
notes: OAC collection guide for the John Muir Papers (Mss48) held by the Holt-Atherton Special Collections, University of the Pacific. Hosted on oac.cdlib.org, which is not in the authority registry, so secondary. Registry proposal: Online Archive of California (oac.cdlib.org), California Digital Library, as institutional.

claim: John Muir studied botany and geology at the University of Wisconsin (1861-1863).

evidence.quote: A Scottish-born journalist and naturalist, John Muir (1838-1914) studied botany and geology at the University of Wisconsin (1861-1863).

claim: John Muir was a Scottish-born journalist and naturalist.

evidence.quote: A Scottish-born journalist and naturalist, John Muir (1838-1914) studied botany and geology at the University of Wisconsin (1861-1863).

notes: IHH lists naturalist, preservationist, writer and inventor; this finding aid gives journalist and naturalist.
